More of the massive spending on AI should shift toward energy infrastructure. AI companies have grown to a point where, if this trajectory continues unchecked, they could place enormous strain on society. It is a race, after all, and many people want the American side to win. But winning the AI race also requires investing in the energy systems needed to support it.

Really good video, from someone who mostly hates AI. I’m a software engineer, and the biggest problem in my industry right now is that, yes, while we’re still needed to be like the pilot, the human at the end to ensure quality, that skill is atrophying. The less we write code, the worse this skill becomes. We’re only good reviewers because we were once producers. We lived in the codebase, in the domain, and we had intricate understandings of things. When you look at generated code exclusively without writing any yourself, you slowly lose the ability to find issues, especially because AI can often get it to work, even if the quality of that solution is poorly done. As long as it technically works, ship it I guess? But eventually, the cost of this is going to explode, and unlike a 3D printer which only needs refills and some light maintenance, the cost is paid for. The next time you need to 3D print a pyramid, the cost won’t change randomly. It won’t get it wrong just because and waste your plastic, causing you to try again. AI being probabilistic is the other issue, and I don’t see it ever being resolved, especially when the cost skyrockets and we’re paying for each run, whether it’s successful or a failure.
